title: File friction after the polish_done event, not before it
body:
**Chose:** `file_friction` runs right after `PolishDone` is emitted, before `polish` returns.
**Over:** between `commit_polish` and the `PolishDone` emit, as the slice's ":325" placement reads.
**Because:** a driver that dies between filing and the event re-enters polish and would file a second `-2` idea; after the event, a death files nothing, which FR-7 already accepts.
**Undo:** move the one call line above `run.emit(EventKind::PolishDone …)`.

title: init output when the skills or one convention file were not written
body:
**Chose:** the commit subject carries `(skills <version>)` only when `init` rendered the skills this run; otherwise it is `chore: factory init`. When `CLAUDE.md` links to `AGENTS.md`, the `convention block:` line and the `git add` list name the link's target (`AGENTS.md`), not the link.
**Over:** always printing the version in the subject (a lie on a source checkout or a repo whose skills `update` owns); naming the link, which `git add` would stage unchanged while the real edit went uncommitted.
**Because:** the slice fixed the full-run output but was silent on partial runs; the printed line must commit exactly what changed.
**Undo:** `src/docs/scaffold.rs` `init` (`subject`) and `convention` (`shown`).

title: review second: renames, an empty diff, and killing the reviewer's group
body:
**Chose:** `--no-renames` on the numstat and on each pass's diff, so a rename is a delete plus an add and every path is one plain file name; an empty diff against the base prints `unreviewed: no changes against <base>` and exits 2; each child runs in its own process group and a timeout SIGKILLs the group; the probe's output goes to `list-models.txt` in the log dir and `log: <dir>` follows an `unreviewed:` line too.
**Over:** parsing `old => new` numstat paths; exit 0 on nothing to review; killing only the direct child, which leaves a wrapper script's node process running and spending quota.
**Because:** the slice was silent on all four; each is the choice that cannot read as a clean review or leak a reviewer.
**Undo:** drop `--no-renames` in `src/review.rs` `numstat`/`diff`; change the early return in `src/cli/review.rs`; remove `process_group(0)` and the `libc::kill` line in `run_logged`.

title: tests/review.rs runs the stub at a 20 s timeout except the timeout test
body:
**Chose:** `[review] timeout_secs = 2` only in `a_timeout_keeps_the_partial_text`; the other fixtures write 20.
**Over:** 2 s in every fixture, as the slice's acceptance line reads.
**Because:** the probe and every pass run under the same timeout, so a node start-up slowed by a parallel `cargo test` past 2 s would turn a replay into a kill and flake the three-pass test. The timeout behaviour itself is still proven at 2 s.
**Undo:** pass 2 to `fixture(...)` in every test.

title: src/config.rs holds slice 05's [source] beside [review]
body:
**Chose:** add `[review]` on top of the working tree's `src/config.rs`, which already carried slice 05's uncommitted `[source]` (`TOP_KEYS` now lists both, as the slice said the two lines merge).
**Over:** reverting slice 05's lines to keep this slice's diff pure.
**Because:** the slice-05 commit (393ddbd) left `src/closeout.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/docs/preflight.rs` and `tests/stubs/claude` modified in the tree; removing them would break slice 05. This slice's commit may therefore carry slice 05's `[source]` hunks.
**Undo:** none needed; split the hunks by hand if the history matters.

title: slice 07 writes the integer version parser that slice 03 now uses, and shares src/skills.rs with it
body:
**Chose:** `skills::version_parts` (three `u64`s, `None` on anything else, pre-release suffixes included) written in this slice; slice 03, building beside it in another lane, already calls it from `verdict_for`. This slice's `src/skills.rs` therefore sits in one file with slice 03's uncommitted `Version`, `Verdict` and `remove_dropped` hunks, and whichever slice commits first carries both.
**Over:** waiting for slice 03's parser, which the slice assumed existed but did not exist when this slice started.
**Because:** the two slices ran at once; one parser is what both slices asked for.
**Undo:** none needed; split the `src/skills.rs` hunks by hand if the history matters.

title: the bundle lock is read once per test binary through a OnceLock
body:
**Chose:** `tests/skills_bundle.rs` reads, checks, or (with `FACTORY_BUNDLE_WRITE`) rewrites the lock once inside a `OnceLock`, and both `bundle_lock_matches` and the manifest test use that result.
**Over:** each test reading the lock file on its own.
**Because:** cargo runs the two in parallel, so the manifest test could read a half-written lock during a write run.
**Undo:** inline the helper into `bundle_lock_matches` and read the file in the manifest test.

title: skills update on an unreadable manifest, and manifest paths outside the skills dirs
body:
**Chose:** `factory skills update` on an `unreadable` manifest prints the doctor line and exits 1, writing nothing; `remove_dropped` skips any old-manifest path that is not plain names (no `..`, no root) and any `[links]` key outside `.agents/skills/`.
**Over:** re-rendering over an unreadable manifest (the dropped files would be invisible), or deleting whatever path a hand-written manifest names.
**Because:** the slice was silent on both; each choice cannot delete a file outside the two skills dirs or lose track of what the old bundle held.
**Undo:** `src/cli/skills.rs` `update` (the `Verdict::Unreadable` arm) and `src/skills.rs` `plain`.

title: src/skills.rs is shared with slice 07, building beside this slice
body:
**Chose:** add the verdict, `read_manifest` and `remove_dropped` to `src/skills.rs` next to slice 07's uncommitted `Lock`, `version_parts`, `check_lock` and `relock`, and compare versions with slice 07's `version_parts`, not a second parser.
**Over:** a private version parser in this slice, or reverting slice 07's lines to keep this diff pure.
**Because:** `state.toml` shows slice 07 building in lane 2 on the same tree, and it had already written a `version_parts` that does exactly FR-3's integer comparison. The working tree also carries slice 07's `Cargo.toml` bump to 0.2.0; every test here builds versions from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, so it passes either way.
**Undo:** none needed; this slice's commit may carry slice 07's `src/skills.rs` hunks, or slice 07's may carry these.

title: Release machinery: a CI workflow and three Cargo.toml additions written for FR-8
body:
**Chose:** commit the `dist generate` output `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a CI workflow file, which an unattended run otherwise never writes) and `dist-workspace.toml`; add `repository = "https://github.com/emilianotisato/factory"`, `[package.metadata.dist] dist = true` and dist's `[profile.dist]` to `Cargo.toml`; `tokio` (`rt`) as a direct dependency for the `--check` runtime, already in the tree through `axoupdater`'s `blocking`.
**Over:** leaving the workflow for the owner, or keeping `[workspace.metadata.dist]` in `Cargo.toml` by hand against what dist 0.32 writes.
**Because:** FR-8 orders the workflow, and the PRD outranks the never-list for a file it names; dist refuses to plan a `publish = false` package without `dist = true`, and the GitHub host needs `repository`. The workflow is unproven until the owner's first tag.
**Undo:** delete `release.yml` and `dist-workspace.toml`, and the three `Cargo.toml` additions.

title: The worker hook reads any 'push' in a Bash command as git push
body: A Bash command whose text holds `push` (a Rust `out.push(` in a heredoc) is refused as a git push by the worker hook; write the script to a scratch file with Write and run it.

title: The nine .claude/skills links are staged but no driver commit has taken them
body:
**Chose:** leave the nine `.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../skills/<name>` symlinks (`_shared`, `deliver`, `gate`, `harness`, `polish`, `prd`, `prune`, `slice`, `ux`) staged, fix the cause in `src/commit.rs` (`Pathspec::from_stream` now tests for a dir without following a symlink), and ask the owner to commit them by hand before CI runs: `git commit -m "chore(004): commit source-checkout skill links" -- .claude/skills/_shared .claude/skills/deliver .claude/skills/gate .claude/skills/harness .claude/skills/polish .claude/skills/prd .claude/skills/prune .claude/skills/slice .claude/skills/ux`.
**Over:** blocking the run here, or committing them from the worker (the contract forbids a worker commit).
**Because:** the installed driver counts each link as a directory (`is_dir` follows the link), so slice-01's commit and both checkpoint commits swept nothing under it, and its baseline filter drops the links from the polish commit too. Without them `tests/skills_bundle.rs` `this_repos_claude_skills_link_into_the_source` fails in CI. The fix only helps a driver built from this branch.
**Undo:** none needed once committed; `git rm --cached` the nine paths to drop them.

title: When render refuses a symlinked layout, does init still write the docs layout?
body:
**Chose:** `init` renders the skills first, before `docs/`, `project.toml` and the convention block, so a refused layout leaves the repo exactly as it was.
**Over:** keeping the old order, where `docs/` and `project.toml` were already written when the skills refusal surfaced.
**Because:** the refusal says "nothing written"; a half-initialised repo next to that message is a lie, and a re-run after fixing the link would then report a partial `created` line. Output order is unchanged: printing still happens after all writes.
**Undo:** move the `rendered` block in `src/docs/scaffold.rs` `init` back below the `.gitignore` step.

title: What do init and skills update print and stage when `.agents/skills` is shared?
body:
**Chose:** the summary reads `skills <v>: .claude/skills/ (19 files, factory.toml), .agents/skills/ is .claude/skills/ (no links)`, and the commit line stages `.claude/skills` only (`Rendered::summary` / `Rendered::dirs`, shared by both commands).
**Over:** printing `(0 links)` and keeping `.agents/skills` in `git add`.
**Because:** `(0 links)` reads like a failure; and `git add .agents/skills` fails outright ("beyond a symbolic link") when `.agents` itself is the link. The shared link is the owner's file, not something factory wrote.
**Undo:** make `Rendered::summary` and `Rendered::dirs` in `src/skills.rs` ignore `shared`.

title: Does a dangling `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` (no `AGENTS.md` yet) count as skipped?
body:
**Chose:** a dangling link is skipped on its turn, but after both files are handled any skip that now resolves inside the repo and holds the heading is dropped, so `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` with no `AGENTS.md` prints only `convention block: AGENTS.md`. A dangling skip says `(a dangling link)`, an outside one `(links outside the repo)`.
**Over:** reporting every dangling link as `links outside the repo`, including the in-repo pair that ends up correct.
**Because:** that pair is the FR-2 linked-pair layout before its first file exists; the block does land once through `AGENTS.md`, and a skip line for it would be false.
**Undo:** delete the `skipped.retain(...)` step at the end of `convention()` in `src/docs/scaffold.rs`.

title: Does the layout check leave `.claude/skills` behind when it refuses?
body:
**Chose:** `layout()` creates `.claude/skills` (to canonicalize it against `.agents/skills`), and when it then refuses a symlinked `.agents` or `.agents/skills` it removes the empty `.claude/skills` and `.claude` it created.
**Over:** leaving an empty `.claude/skills` behind on refusal.
**Because:** keeps "nothing written" literally true; `remove_dir` only removes empty dirs, so nothing pre-existing can go.
**Undo:** drop the two `remove_dir` calls in `layout()` in `src/skills.rs`.

title: Which side is blamed when both the manifest's and the binary's versions fail to parse?
body:
**Chose:** the manifest is checked first, so both bad reports `unreadable .claude/skills/factory.toml: version "…" is not three integers`; only a good manifest with a bad binary prints `binary version … is not three integers`. `Verdict::Unreadable` now carries the whole line.
**Over:** blaming the binary first.
**Because:** keeps the existing manifest message byte-identical; the binary case still surfaces once the manifest is fixed.
**Undo:** swap the two `let … else` checks in `verdict_for` in `src/skills.rs`.

title: Does a non-zero exit's partial text count as reviewed?
body:
**Chose:** No. The assistant text of a run that exited non-zero with no `result` is printed under `(exit <code>, partial)` (or `(killed by a signal, partial)`) and the pass stays unreviewed; when no other pass returned text the command exits 2 and the skills' fallback starts.
**Over:** counting it like a timeout's partial, which FR-6 counts.
**Because:** a timeout's partial comes from a reviewer that worked the whole timeout; a non-zero exit is a crash, an auth or a rate-limit failure, usually early, and its text is often only the opening "I'll read the diff". Counting it is the failure F7 names: exit 0 and no review at all. Not counting it costs at worst one redundant fallback review, and the text is still printed for triage, so nothing is lost.
**Undo:** in `body` (`src/cli/review.rs`), return `true` for the partial branch of `Ended::Exited`; flip the `false` expectations in `each_ending_has_its_marker_and_only_text_that_finished_counts` and `a_non_zero_exit_marks_its_partial_and_does_not_count`.

title: What an error `result` with assistant text before it prints
body:
**Chose:** `unreviewed (exit <code>, error: <text>)`, then the assistant text under `(exit <code>, partial)`; not counted. A `result` with `is_error: true` is kept in `Parsed::error`, never in `result`.
**Over:** the error line alone, with the partial text left in the log only.
**Because:** a rate limit hit late in a long pass leaves real findings in the partial text; printing them under a partial header costs nothing, and the `unreviewed` line keeps the pass out of the reviewed count.
**Undo:** drop the `match partial` append after an error in `body`.

title: Signal forwarding: re-raise, and leave an inherited ignore alone
body:
**Chose:** the handler for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP kills the reviewer's group with SIGKILL, restores the default disposition and re-raises, so factory dies of the same signal; it is installed once per process before the first spawn and not installed for a signal factory started out ignoring (`nohup`, a background job).
**Over:** `_exit(130)` for every signal, and installing over an inherited ignore.
**Because:** re-raising keeps the wait status a shell or `/deliver` expects (`SIGTERM`, not exit 130), and `nohup factory review second` must still survive a closed terminal as the user asked. The handler stays installed between passes; with no reviewer running it only re-raises, which is the default behaviour.
**Undo:** in `forward` (`src/review.rs`) replace the `signal`/`raise` pair with `libc::_exit(128 + sig)`; drop the `SIG_IGN` check in `forward_signals`.

title: Where the orphan polish path gets the config `file_friction` reads
body:
**Chose:** `closeout::settle_orphan` loads the config itself (`config::load_with_project`, the driver's own read) right after `PolishDone`, and files nothing when the load fails.
**Over:** threading the driver's `&Config` through `scheduler::settle_orphans` into `settle_orphan`.
**Because:** `src/scheduler.rs` is outside this fixer's files while two sibling fixers share the tree; `[source]` is user-scope only and nothing in the run overrides it, so a fresh read sees the same value, and a config gone unreadable mid-run should not fail the orphan's settle when the live path would only have skipped filing.
**Undo:** add `cfg: &Config` to `scheduler::settle_orphans` and `closeout::settle_orphan` (both callers in `scheduler::drive` hold one) and pass it to `file_friction` in place of the load.

title: Whether the hand `proceed` to a dead polish files friction
body:
**Chose:** leave it as it is: the `proceed` path (`polish_by_hand` in `closeout::run`) files nothing.
**Over:** filing from `retro.md` on the pass that first sees the `proceed`.
**Because:** it is not the orphan's omission. There the driver made the polish commit and dropped the step after it; here the owner ran `/polish` and committed by hand, and FR-7 files "after the polish commit" the driver makes. Every later closeout pass sees `polish_by_hand` again, and no event marks a filing, so a ship that parks and resumes would file a second `-2` idea; filing once needs a new event, which is more than a polish fix.
**Undo:** emit a `friction_filed` event from `file_friction`, and on a `polish_by_hand` pass with none in the log, call `file_friction` before `ship`.

title: What a `[source]` without a usable `path` loads as
body:
**Chose:** a `[source]` with no string `path` (no key, a number, or `source = "…"` as a bare value) is removed from the table before the typed read: it loads as no `[source]` and warns ``[source]` has no `path` string, ignored``; `SourceRepo { path: PathBuf }` stays as callers use it.
**Over:** making `SourceRepo::path` an `Option`, which every caller (`closeout`, `cli/upgrade`) would then unwrap.
**Because:** the module contract is "a warning, never an error", and no `[source]` already means "file nothing, no upgrade source" everywhere.
**Undo:** delete `drop_pathless_source` and its call in `config::load`.

title: Skills render refuses a symlinked .claude, .claude/skills, .agents or .agents/skills
body:
**Chose:** `skills::render` (so `factory init` and `factory skills update`) refuses, writing nothing, when `.claude`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents` or `.agents/skills` is a symlink or not a directory; when `.agents/skills` resolves to `.claude/skills` it writes the files and no links. `init` also skips a `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` that links outside the repo, with a `convention block: skipped …` line.
**Over:** following the links, as the slice built it.
**Because:** a cloned repo controls those paths; following them writes, and `skills update` deletes, outside the repo. FR-2's "collisions are not special-cased" covers a real dir where a link goes, not a redirected parent.
**Undo:** remove the `layout()` check in `src/skills.rs` and the outside-repo skip in `convention()` in `src/docs/scaffold.rs`.

title: CI gate red: the nine .claude/skills links were never committed
body:
**Happened:** CI's clean checkout of HEAD (d9112e9) has no `.claude/skills/`, so `tests/skills_bundle.rs` `this_repos_claude_skills_link_into_the_source` panics at `tests/skills_bundle.rs:60:62` with `prd: No such file or directory (os error 2)`. Reproduced in a detached worktree of HEAD (4 passed, 1 failed); the inner loop is green on this machine only because the nine links sit staged in the working tree. This is the AD-11 gap: the installed driver treats each link as a directory and its baseline filter drops paths dirty before the worker started, so a CI fix worker's files cannot carry them, and a worker may not commit.
**Options:**
1. Owner commits the staged links by hand, then the driver re-runs CI: `git commit -m "chore(004): commit source-checkout skill links" -- .claude/skills/_shared .claude/skills/deliver .claude/skills/gate .claude/skills/harness .claude/skills/polish .claude/skills/prd .claude/skills/prune .claude/skills/slice .claude/skills/ux` and push `feat/skills`. Cost: one manual commit.
2. Rebuild the driver from this branch (`cargo install --path .`, which carries the `Pathspec::from_stream` symlink fix) and retry the fix round. Cost: the baseline filter may still drop the pre-staged links, so this can fail the same way.
3. Make the test skip when `.claude/skills` is absent. Cost: weakens the check FR-1 relies on; forbidden to get green.
**Recommended:** 1.
Commit only the nine staged .claude/skills symlinks on feat/skills (pathspec .claude/skills), push the branch, and rerun CI.

title: Who commits the nine .claude/skills links BLOCK-1's answer ordered
body:
**Chose:** the round-2 CI fix worker ran BLOCK-1's option 1 itself, with the owner's pathspec only: `git commit -m "chore(004): commit source-checkout skill links" -- .claude/skills/{_shared,deliver,gate,harness,polish,prd,prune,slice,ux}`. The driver pushes it after the round. The full gate in a clean worktree of the new HEAD: rc 0, 87 s.
**Over:** blocking again, or leaving the links to the fix commit.
**Because:** the answer (2026-10-13T22:48:16Z) orders exactly this commit, but nobody made it and HEAD stayed d9112e9. The running driver (installed 09:36, before the `Pathspec::from_stream` symlink fix) classes each link as a dir. Its baseline also drops paths dirty at spawn, so the fix commit could never carry them.
**Undo:** `git revert` the `chore(004): commit source-checkout skill links` commit.
